🇲🇽🌎 <u>Guatemala's President Thanks Mexico, Land of Asylum, 72 Years After the CIA Coup</u>

On Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco's first visit to Guatemala, President Bernardo Arévalo unveiled a plaque at the old Mexican embassy. After the 1954 CIA-backed coup, that building sheltered more than 300 people persecuted by the new regime, including the overthrown president, Jacobo Árbenz. Arévalo, himself the son of an exile in Mexico, called the plaque an act of memory, gratitude and brotherhood. Velasco brought greetings from Sheinbaum and said asylum is one of the deepest convictions of Mexico's foreign policy. From Spain's Republicans in 1939 to Guatemala in 1954, the door stayed open.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Treason Charge for the Chihuahua Prosecutor Who Brought the CIA In</u>

Mexico's Attorney General Ernestina Godoy says César Jáuregui, Maru Campos's former state prosecutor, may have committed treason against the nation. The FGR found he organized the April raid on a drug lab in El Pinal, Chihuahua, with CIA agents taking part, kept federal authorities in the dark, and stayed in contact with US officials the whole time. Two of those agents died in a crash on the way back. After more than 100 investigative acts, a federal judge issued the warrant. In Godoy's words, it "violates the sovereignty and integrity of the nation, as it is expressly prohibited."
banner: CIA CASE: EX-PROSECUTOR CHARGED W/ TREASON

🇲🇽📉 <u>Mexico's Lowest Year-to-Date Inflation Since 2020, and Three States Where Prices Fell</u>

According to INEGI, consumer prices rose 2.12% from January to September 2026, the smallest increase for that period since 2020. Sonora (-0.58%), Baja California Sur (-0.43%) and Sinaloa (-0.20%) were the only states where prices fell. The main reason was electricity, through CFE's subsidized hot-season tariffs. Eggs were the second-biggest drag on prices. Jalisco had the highest rate in the country, at 3.88%.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN Rolls Out the Welcome Mat for Cabeza de Vaca in 2027</u>

PAN national leader Jorge Romero says it "would be an honor" for former Tamaulipas governor Francisco García Cabeza de Vaca to run for Congress in 2027. Romero insists there is no arrest warrant against him and calls the organized-crime and money-laundering investigations "political persecution." This is PAN's plan to win back Tamaulipas.
banner: PAN OPENS 2027 DOOR TO CABEZA DE VACA

🔥🇲🇽 <u>A $760 Million Pemex Fraud From the Peña Nieto Years Still Has No Charges</u>

In 2013, José Manuel Carrera Panizzo, then head of PMI Comercio Internacional, signed the deal to buy the scrap-metal Agro Nitrogenados fertilizer plant from Alonso Ancira. Pemex puts the damage at more than 760 million dollars. Contralínea reports that the FGR's anti-corruption office still hasn't taken the case to a judge and is claiming only 309 million. Emilio Lozoya and his sister would also benefit if the case collapses. The FGR answered that the statute of limitations runs to July 2028, and that it will file "in short order."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico's Senate Moves to Bring US Lawmakers to the Table on T-MEC and Migrants</u>

Ignacio Mier, who heads the Senate's governing board, says an interparliamentary meeting with US Congress members is viable. The agenda would cover the T-MEC review, security and protection for Mexicans in the US. The Senate is preparing its own invitation, alongside the Chamber of Deputies' work with the House. Mier said parliamentary diplomacy can "complement" the government's foreign policy and Mexico's consular network. In May 2025, a Senate delegation went to Washington to fight the proposed tax on remittances.
banner: SENATE INVITES US CONGRESS: T-MEC TALKS

🇲🇽🐄 <u>No Foot-and-Mouth in Sonora: Cattle Exports to the US Resume Tuesday</u>

Mexico's animal-health agency Senasica finished its lab tests on the calf that had stopped cattle crossings at Agua Prieta–Douglas. The result is bovine papular stomatitis, a mild disease with no public-health risk, and foot-and-mouth disease is ruled out. Exports to the United States restart on Tuesday.

text: 🇲🇽✊ "Something a ruler has to do is listen." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Umán, Yucatán She is touring IMSS-Bienestar hospitals and health centers, and drops in on health centers unannounced — not even the governor or the mayor is told — because "when they say the president is coming, they fix everything, they paint it." She talks with patients and pharmacy staff, then meets hospital directors: "Total frankness." In Quintana Roo on Friday, the directors of all three hospitals told her they are better off with IMSS-Bienestar than before. Specialist appointments are up about 36% since 2024, and IMSS-Bienestar care is free.

🔥🇲🇽 "Do you know how much they owe now? Zero. They owe nothing." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Umán, Yucatán She walked through three Yucatán cases. Julián Rodríguez borrowed 55,000 pesos for a home, had paid 218,000, and in 2024 owed one million. Miriam Elizabeth Chablé Arana borrowed 63,000, paid 380,000, owed 2,084,000. María Ortiz Chan borrowed 88,000, paid 277,000, owed one million. López Obrador froze Infonavit evictions and changed how loans were granted; her government restructured the old loans — more than 5 million of them.
banner: INFONAVIT DEBTS: FROM 1M PESOS TO ZERO

text: 🔥🇲🇽 "Infonavit was a loan-shark bank — no, you fell short, governor. They were thieves." — Octavio Romero Oropeza, director general of Infonavit, Umán, Yucatán Governor Joaquín Díaz Mena had thanked the president for changing Infonavit so it is "never again a loan-shark institution." Romero explained why: on top of interest and principal, Infonavit added the yearly minimum-wage increase to the balance, so debts rose even as people paid. 4,856,000 of these "unpayable" loans were restructured as of December 31 — 136,000 in Yucatán. Borrowers who finished paying but never released the mortgage lien, a procedure costing 16,000–18,000 pesos, now get it free: 84,000 families in Yucatán.
